independence_declaration.statement: In this run qa-verifier wrote no product implementation in the DG7 scope and changed no candidate file. The implementer roles listed wrote the product, tooling, guides and register; the orchestrator froze the candidate, regenerated release notes and known limitations, and ran the A26/A27 drills and the container host run. Earlier qa-verifier authoring tasks (T-DG7-QA-B to F) wrote acceptance tests under tests/qa/** before the freeze; they are tests, not implementation, and I judged them here as a reviewer (re-ran them, probed beyond them, and found the A26 regression gap they do not cover). Every execution ran in disposable clones under $TMPDIR (removed at the end) and disposable PostgreSQL clusters; my own probes are in my evidence directory, none in the candidate. I formed this verdict without reading any other reviewer's round-1 record. Two run-record commits by the other reviewers (6c66c0157, 855de9e2d) landed during my run; I did not open their records. A validator loop I had stopped kept running and wrote --reconcile and --stage DG7 logs at HEAD 6c66c015, which could show another reviewer's verdict; I moved both files out of my evidence directory unread and re-ran reconcile on a clone of the freeze commit instead. Assignment deviations, stated rather than guessed: (1) the assignment asks for round 7, but the record lives in round-1 and the validator requires rec.round to equal the directory round (tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs l.682, l.794), so round is 1; (2) the template it names, docs/delivery/reviews/DG5/round-3/qa-verifier.json, does not exist; I mirrored DG5 round-2 and DG6 round-1; (3) it limits finding owners to implementer roles, but two of my findings concern orchestrator-only records (the freeze commit, progress.md); I used owner delivery-orchestrator, which findings.schema.json allows and F-DG6-911 used.
